prerequisites: Completion of the Psychology of Education, Pedagogy I, Pedagogy II courses
Psychopedagogical communication, relationship, and evaluation competencies

learning_outcomes.text: Argue the relationships between teaching-learning-evaluation and formulate creative solutions for optimizing educational components.
Correlate specialized psychopedagogical knowledge in carrying out instructional-educational activities in education and other educational activities.
Argue the formative potential of theories, principles, and didactic practices specific to the field.
Identify the specific way in which children/students/youth learn, theories, counseling paradigms supporting learning, and their implications for teaching and evaluation.
Analyze and correlate psychopedagogical knowledge in continuous professional development and improvement activities.
Identify the specific demands and rigors of responsible use of new technologies in varied didactic situations.
Identify the level of previous acquisitions of children/students/youth, individually and in groups, and utilize the obtained data in designing the educational process.
Identify learning objectives in accordance with curricular documents that support the development of each child/student/youth's potential.
Construct authentic learning contexts, in an integrated manner, in which students utilize their life experiences and knowledge interests.
Select scientifically founded techniques for group cohesion construction, socio-emotional development, and for behavior management.
Periodically participate in continuous professional development activities, in relation to their own professional needs and local or national priorities.
Critically approach the responsibilities of the teaching profession, highlighting the complexity of the educational process.
Develop creative and constructive attitudes in applying pedagogical design and principles.
Indicate the necessity of using varied resources to enhance teaching, support learning, and assist students in their autonomous use.
Communicate efficiently by providing constructive feedback and actively supporting students' involvement in their own learning process.
Defend/Respect the ethnic, socio-economic, linguistic, and religious diversity of students and their communities of origin, managing their implications for learning development.
Support the socio-emotional and moral development of students.
Support family/guardians to understand expectations and their role, collaborating with them for students' educational success.
Combine interrogative and reflexive approaches regarding professional practice and engagement in professional training and continuous education activities.
Accept managerial roles specific to education. Identify various types of decisions and educational resources needed in different specific educational contexts.
Support a democratic culture of learning and collaboration at the group/class and institutional levels.
Maintain a positive atmosphere in class and school, cultivating belonging to the educational community.
Display/Manifest professional balance and adaptability in different contexts, including new or stressful situations, while maintaining appropriate authority in relation to educational persons/groups.

syllabus_topics: Concept of management. Orientations and managerial schools. Concept of management; term, meanings, educational management, classroom management. Orientations and managerial schools: definition and evolution.
Types of managerial cultures. Organizational culture: definition, components. Types of organizational cultures. Managerial culture in an educational context.
Managerial activities of the teacher. Conceptual delimitations. Explanatory theories and managerial roles of the teaching staff. Dimensional structure of classroom management.
The classroom as a primary group. Types of psychosocial groups. Characterization of the small psychosocial group. Methods, techniques, and procedures for understanding the classroom.

Psychosocial climate and phenomena of group dynamics. Group dynamics: definition, facilitating and hindering factors of group dynamics. Psychosocial climate dimensions. Communication and conflict in the classroom.

The teacher as counselor, the guidance lesson. Definition. Competencies of the teacher-counselor. Digital competencies in exercising the teacher's managerial roles. Platforms, methods, techniques for working with students.
Thematic review for the exam. Review of the main topics covered in the course. Discussion of exam topics.
Conceptual differentiations: management, educational management, classroom management. Evolution of managerial schools from classic to current management. Case studies.
Types of managerial cultures: power culture, role culture, task culture, personal culture - Worksheets.
Designing, planning, organizing, deciding, coordinating, leading, evaluating, counseling as managerial roles and activities of the teacher. Worksheets.
Relationships and interactions in the classroom: inter-knowledge relationships, inter-communication relationships, preferential socio-affective relationships, influence relationships - Worksheets.
The classroom as a primary group: characteristics - debate.
Understanding the classroom: observation, questionnaire, test, experiment, sociometric methods, analysis of activity products. Teacher's notebook.

Change management, effective behavior management, design management, activity organization management, influencing and motivating management, communication management, relationship management, evaluation management. Worksheets.
assessment_rules: The final grade must be a minimum of 5. The exam and applications each contribute 50% to the final grade.
